exactness_argument.fieldops: None of them changes what is computed; each changes how: F1. **Inlined field products and squares** (`fast_field`, `fmul`, `fsqr`). The library's `Gf2_128::mul` folds with its `clmul_u64`, which is not `#[inline]` and lives in the library crate, so every product makes six out-of-line calls (round 2's C8 enabled the carry-less multiply in the state loop but could not inline that call). `fast_field::mul` forms the same polynomial product with four carry-less 64 x 64 products (the library's Karatsuba uses three; both give the one product of the two polynomials) and reduces it with the library's two folds by the tail t = irr - z^n, statement for statement (`reduce` is `reduce_fold`). `fast_field::sqr` forms a0^2 + a1^2 z^128, the square in characteristic 2, and the same reduction. A reduced field element is unique, so every product and square is the library's. Side B's binary is built with `-C target-feature=+pclmulqdq` (`online-b/.cargo/config.toml`) so the carry-less products inline. `fast_field::check` runs before any use and fails closed: the CPU has the instruction, the field meets the library's fold conditions (tail degree d <= 63, 2d < n + 2, n + d <= 129), and the inlined product and square equal the library's on edge cases and on 65,536 pseudo-random pairs. E1. **The state loop's three squarings by the inlined square.** `s3_roots_from_inverses` read `solver.square`, a byte-table map built by `S3Solver128::new` from the images `gf.sqr(e)` of the unit vectors. Squaring is GF(2)-linear and the table map is the linear map with those images, so the two agree on every element; its 45 KB of tables leave the state loop's cache footprint. E2. **Byte-image lookups for every linear map** (`Linear128::apply`). The same eleven table lookups of the same tables and the same XORs, with the bytes read from `v.to_le_bytes()` instead of eleven variable shifts of v. S4. **The scan self-test evaluated from per-round tables** (`RoundTables`). `ScanPermutation::apply` calls `round(right, key)` only with right = (index & mask) < 2^half, and every later right is masked again, so each round is read from a table of `round(v, key)` over [0, 2^half), filled by calling `round` itself. The table-evaluated `apply` is therefore `apply` on every index, and `scan_permutation_selftest` makes the parent's three checks (no image at or above the domain, no repeated in-range image, exactly `len` in-range images) of the same function over the same domain in the same order, with the parent's eight-image loop. The online and rank scans still evaluate `apply`; the self-test's sampled inverse check is unchanged. Two more edits: the header comment and the summary field `field_ops_pipeline` (this producer's name for the four changes; side A's binary emits none). One appended test module (`fieldops_tests`, run by the workflow's `cargo test --bins`) checks the equalities the proofs above rest on: the inlined product and square against the library's on every pair of a 2^20-element sample and on edge cases, the square map against the inlined square, the byte-image lookup against the parent's shift loop, and the table-evaluated permutation against `apply` on every index of the M38 and M10 domains for both self-test keys.

parent.indexbuild2: The round-2 producer differs from the row's in two computations, neither of which changes a value. (C9) State loop: for a regular state (l != r, l != 0, r != 0; exactly the states whose parent denominator a*ps is non-zero, since squaring is injective and GF(2^83) has no zero divisors) the parent computes a = (l+r)^2, p = l r, ps = p^2, c = ps + b, inv = (a ps)^-1, q = p (ps inv) = p/a and d = (c a)(a inv) = c a/ps. The round-2 loop computes q = p ((l+r)^-1)^2 and d = c (l^-1 + r^-1)^2, the same field elements because a/ps = ((l+r)/(l r))^2 = (1/l + 1/r)^2. Every inverse is a field inverse (1/l and 1/r: the inverse of a representative squared k times is the inverse of its k-th Frobenius shift, each checked by a product at build time; 1/(l+r): Montgomery's trick over four interleaved chains, the inverse of a non-zero element being unique), and field elements have one reduced representation, so q and d are bit for bit the parent's; the trace test, the half trace, the root order and the to_normal images then are the parent's. An irregular state takes s3_x_roots_128(gf, b, l, r), which is what the parent's finish returns for a zero denominator. States are pushed in the parent's (left, right, relative) order, so stored_states_blake3 is the parent's. (C7) Insert loop: for a nonconstant 83-bit word v, z_1 = !v and z_(j+1) = z_j & rotl(z_j, 1) has bit p set iff bits p..p-j are zero (cyclically), so the last nonzero z_j is Z_L (L the longest zero run), the tops of all longest zero runs, which is the run set lift_scan's greedy lifting ends with (lift2/src/lib.rs). The candidate rotations s = N-1-p and the choice (least rotation, ties to the smaller shift, an order-independent minimum) are lift_scan's, and 0 and the all-ones word return shift 0 as in lift_scan; so the key and shift equal lift_scan's for every word. In the eight-lane form a lane that reaches its Z_L keeps it by a select while the other lanes continue; the word 0 starts at z = 0. Keys are computed once per root in increasing root order (eight at a time, the tail one at a time by the parent's call), the planted counter is incremented once per root in lift_plant, the prefetch is a hint, and insert_if_absent receives the parent's (key, value) sequence, so every slot word, and table_slots_blake3, is the parent's. Relations, probes, the rank stage and the online scan read only the index and the self-test verdict, so they are the parent's. Checked locally on every stored root of K600, M38 and M10 (inputs/local_exactness.json) and gated per process and per base in the run.

parent.indexbuild: The derived producer differs from the row's in three computations, none of which changes a value. (1) State loop: S3Solver128::roots computes prepare, one inversion of the denominator a*ps (zero takes the scalar fallback) and finish. RootBatch128::solve computes the same prepare, inverts the product of the row's non-zero denominators once and recovers each inverse as (prefix product) x (inverse of the running product), which is that denominator's field inverse because inverses in GF(2^83) are unique; finish then returns the same two roots in the same order. States are pushed in the parent's (left, right, relative) order, so stored_states_blake3 is the parent's. (2) Insert loop: index_canonical128 is a pure function of the root (plus the planted counter, called once per root in the same order), so computing it 32 roots early changes no key or shift; the prefetch is a hint without architectural effect; insert_if_absent is called with the same (key, value) sequence into the same table, so every slot word, and table_slots_blake3, is the parent's. (3) Self-test: the parent returns false iff some image of [0, domain) is >= domain or an in-range image repeats, else visited == len; the lanes loop evaluates the same apply on the same indices and the same checks on the images in index order, eight applies ahead of their checks, so it returns the same boolean. Relations, probes, the rank stage and the online scan read only the index and the self-test verdict, so they are the parent's. Gated per process and per base on K600, M38 and M10.
parent.parent: Frobenius phi acts on the prime-order subgroup as multiplication by lambda (lambda^2 - lambda + 2 = 0 mod r), so for alpha = a + b tau, alpha(R) = [a]R + [b]phi(R) = [(a + b lambda) mod r]R, and every member +-phi^k(alpha(R_c)) of orbit (c, alpha) has discrete log +-(a + b lambda) lambda^k log R_c. The header carries exactly these labels; verify_closure.py re-derives every member and label from the orbit representative and checks each representative against [w]R_c and, with the table, against [w L_c]G, in the pinned oracle. A relation found by the unchanged S3 search is checked in the group by the unchanged lift (four base points summing to the attempt's point), so its row sum_i coeff_i L_{c_i} = a (+ L_c for the guided column) holds exactly; full rank gives the unique logs, checked [L_c]G = R_c in process and equal to B's archived logs of the same R_c. A target's scalar is checked [d]G = Q in process and replayed in the oracle, and must equal the baseline's and the tuned rho's. The root index, probe loop and scan are the rank-probe producer's code, built from the closure's orbit representatives. With KIC_INDEX_CANON=lift the index build keys every stored state's two normal-basis roots with lift_scan instead of the selected canonicalizer; both return the least rotation of the 83-bit word and the least shift reaching it, the stored states are computed before and independently of that call, so the table receives the same inserts in the same order and its slot array is the same word for word (index-lift's argument). The layout digests gate this per process on every base, so every relation, probe count, rank table and scalar of a lift-built index is the selected-built index's.

parent.rankfinder: The rank-finder producer differs from the row's in one computation, which does not change a value. In scan_state128_frame (KIC_RANK_SOLVE=frame and frame_plant, used only by the rank stage) the parent computes every partner word's key as target_canonical::<CANON_LIFT>, i.e. lift_scan_wide(v, 83), right after the word. The derived loop pushes the same partner words in the same order with the same candidate index and pair starts, and whenever eight keys are pending computes their (canonical, shift) with lift_linear_lanes8::<83>, the parent's own C7 function, whose result equals lift_scan's for every 83-bit word: for a nonconstant word v, z_1 = !v and z_(j+1) = z_j & rotl(z_j, 1) has bit p set iff bits p..p-j are zero (cyclically), so the last nonzero z_j is Z_L, the tops of all longest zero runs, lift_scan's final run set; the candidate rotations and the order-independent choice (least rotation, ties to the smaller shift) are lift_scan's; 0 and the all-ones word give shift 0. The at most seven keys left at the end of a state take the parent's call. Every key is complete before the first lookup, the prefetch is a hint, and the probe loop is the parent's text, so probe positions, the first hit, the relation, root calls and every counter are the parent's. For any other canonicalizer or field size the parent's code runs. Checked by the crate tests against the parent's loop kept verbatim, and locally per seed on M38, M10 and K600 (inputs/local_exactness.json); gated per seed in the run.

question: Is the field-ops producer's END-TO-END cold cost (setup + index build + rank stage + linear algebra + one-target online) on the M38 closure base lower than the current n=83 a=1 row's (the rank-finder producer of koblitz-n83-rankfinder-20261021), on new held-out points and new rank seeds? The stages that change are the index build, the scan self-test, the rank stage and the online stage; every key, probe, relation, root call, counter, index and rank table is the parent's. Side B is built with -C target-feature=+pclmulqdq (online-b/.cargo/config.toml) so the carry-less products inline; side A is built as landed. The test uses repeated alternating pairs and a 95% paired confidence interval whose lower bound must exceed 1 (AGENTS.md, 'CPU performance isolation gate', Tier 1).

statistics.e2e_per_side: E2E(side) = timing_ms.rank_stage of the side's rank process + cold_in_process_ms of the side's cold process: setup (including the index build and the scan self-test) + rank stage + linear algebra + one-target online, the row's definition
statistics.pairing_basis: AGENTS.md Tier 1: 'run both variants on the same pinned exposed CPU with the same workload and limits' and 'require repeated alternating pairs'. A pair is the two variants on the same point with the same rank seed, adjacent in time on one CPU, in alternating order
statistics.primary: R = sum over the 36 primary pairs of E2E(A) / sum over the same pairs of E2E(B). 95% percentile interval from a two-stage paired bootstrap, 10000 draws, random.Random(20261060): the points drawn with replacement, then each drawn point's pairs drawn with replacement; A and B of a pair are always drawn together
statistics.primary_is: the paired END-TO-END ratio over the current row; every stage ratio is co-reported and never decides
secondary: geometric mean of the per-pair ratios E2E(A)/E2E(B), with the same bootstrap
index build, scan self-test, rank stage and online (stage secondaries, labelled), paired
index build in the rank processes kM38RF / kM38FO, paired
E2E process CPU time and process wall A / B, with the same bootstrap
peak RSS and minor faults of the cold processes
per-point ratio, and the ratio by pair position and by side order
probe law of kM38RF and kM38FO; rank ns per probe; rho ms/step from rT; S per side; E2E cold gap RF / rT
statistics.stage_secondary: four STAGE ratios, each labelled a stage secondary and never deciding, in the primary pairs with the same bootstrap: index build (timing_ms.index_build of the cold process) cM38RF / cM38FO, scan self-test (scan_order_selftest.ms of the cold process) cM38RF / cM38FO, rank stage (timing_ms.rank_stage) kM38RF / kM38FO, and online (online_ms of the cold process) cM38RF / cM38FO

success_criterion: AGENTS.md 'Success criterion: iterative improvement of the index-calculus baseline'
tier_rule: AGENTS.md 'CPU performance evidence tiers', Tier 1: same pinned exposed CPU, same workload and limits; code and workload hashes, paired order, raw failures, correctness, process CPU time, memory, cgroup throttling and memory failures, steal time and scheduling counters recorded; repeated alternating pairs and a 95% paired confidence interval whose lower bound exceeds 1
why_this_run: On the parent's run 39527997793 (on main) its side B (this experiment's side A) spent 2.81 of its 7.27 s end to end in the rank stage and 3.25 s of the cold process in the index build, 0.84 s in the scan self-test and 0.16 s in the online stage (means over its 36 primary pairs, inputs/power_prior.json). Each of those stages multiplies in GF(2^83) through the library's out-of-line carry-less product, which is the cost F1 removes; the local profile (inputs/local_profile.json, diagnostic) gives the four stage factors the power check models.
